channel.title: NewsCenter — All newsletter news — 2026-11-28
channel.description: Every news received through Laurent's newsletters over the last 24 hours. 56 news received.

item.title: SAP considers cutting 10,000 jobs in AI-related restructuring
item.description: SAP is considering eliminating at least 10,000 positions, or about 9% of its global workforce, as part of a shift toward artificial intelligence. No final plan has been decided, and discussions with employee representatives are ongoing.

item.title: The best AI models to use in 2026
item.description: The article presents a selection of the best artificial intelligence models to use in 2026.

item.title: The 7 best AI agents for marketing
item.description: The article presents seven artificial intelligence agents designed for marketing activities.

item.title: How to master the best AI tools
item.description: The article explains how to master the best artificial intelligence tools.

item.title: Create AI agents with no prior knowledge
item.description: The article explains how to build artificial intelligence agents with no prior knowledge.

item.title: Moonshot uses Google and Meta models to distill its AI
item.description: The Chinese lab Moonshot is now training its models using responses from Google and Meta systems, after OpenAI and Anthropic strengthened protections against distillation. It is also seeking computing capacity in Europe and from Chinese chipmakers.

item.title: Switzerland confirms the first cyberattacks by AI agents against infrastructure
item.description: Switzerland has confirmed the first cyberattacks carried out by artificial intelligence agents against critical infrastructure.

item.title: Huawei is preparing an AI memory chip to compete with Samsung and SK Hynix
item.description: Huawei has unveiled the beginnings of a memory chip designed for artificial intelligence and intended to compete with Samsung and SK Hynix.

item.title: OpenAI could shift to cost control
item.description: OpenAI could adopt a cost-control strategy.

item.title: Show Projected Range Again as a Number on a Tesla
item.description: On a 2025 Tesla Model 3, projected range was previously displayed numerically. A software update now displays it as a graph.

item.title: Discussion of Model 3 Mechanical and Hardware Issues
item.description: A member describes an issue with their Tesla Model 3 and asks the community for help. The excerpt repeats the question about range display after a software update.

item.title: Nvidia Suspends Server Shipments to Southeast Asia
item.description: Nvidia reportedly asked server manufacturers to halt deliveries to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia after new U.S. export rules took effect. Fitch expects slower growth and more selective investment in the region’s data centers.

item.title: OpenAI’s Chief Scientist Proposes Common Limits for AI
item.description: Jakub Pachocki published the pretraining scores of OpenAI’s main models since GPT-3.5 and asked competing labs to adopt common limits. Sam Altman called the proposal OpenAI’s most important publication in some time.

item.title: Anthropic reportedly limited Claude 5.2 for machine learning work
item.description: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 while deliberately limiting their capabilities in certain areas related to accelerating AI development, including kernel optimization and LLM architecture. The company says agentic coding and traditional machine learning research are unaffected, while no published evidence confirms the sabotage allegations.

item.title: Hackers infiltrate the US Air Force’s main cloud platform
item.description: Hackers exploited a vulnerability to access the control plane of Cloud One, the US Air Force’s cloud platform. The intrusion froze migrations and some software fixes, while US Cyber Command assesses the damage.

item.title: Apple now accounts for 57% of smartphones shipped in the United States
item.description: Apple accounted for 57% of smartphone shipments in the United States in the third quarter of 2026, up from 50% a year earlier. The US market declined 9%, with high memory costs particularly hurting entry-level Android models.

item.title: High-end Nvidia AI chips found at a blacklisted Chinese site
item.description: Nvidia Blackwell processors, which require a US export license to be shipped to China, were found at a Shanghai data center linked to a smuggling case. Chinese documents specifically mention a GB300 NVL72 rack and a GB200 server.

item.title: Soaring memory prices push companies to open “war rooms”
item.description: The global shortage of memory chips is leading small companies in particular to create purchasing teams to search for DRAM, sometimes on eBay. Prices have risen 500%, while manufacturers are prioritizing HBM memory for AI.

item.title: Rockstar employees reject union recognition after GTA VI
item.description: Rockstar employees voted 75% against union recognition, one week after GTA VI was announced.

item.title: Google Play will display some app developers’ home addresses
item.description: Google Play will make the home addresses of some app developers public.

item.title: AI agent makes first UK purchase without a bank card
item.description: An AI agent made a pizza purchase in the United Kingdom without using a bank card, a first according to the article.

item.title: SAP confirms security incident after alleged GitHub hack
item.description: SAP confirmed a security incident after a GitHub hack was reported.

item.title: WhatsApp is preparing an in-app travel eSIM service
item.description: WhatsApp will launch a travel eSIM service directly integrated into its application.

item.title: New cyber incidents hit financial investigators and US spy agencies
item.description: A series of cyber incidents has affected US financial investigators and spy agencies, following a string of hacks and federal outages.

item.title: Cyberattack forces AFP to take its client platform offline
item.description: A cyberattack forced Agence France-Presse to take its platform for clients offline.

item.title: China’s second-largest pork producer turns to robots on its farms
item.description: China’s second-largest pork producer is adopting robots in its livestock buildings.

item.title: Volvo employees train humanoid robots to perform their work
item.description: Volvo employees are teaching humanoid robots to carry out their tasks.

item.title: The Netherlands vows to oppose US bill targeting ASML sales to China
item.description: The Netherlands has pledged to oppose the US bill targeting ASML equipment sales to China.

item.title: Tesla Owners Discuss Range Anxiety
item.description: The exchange focuses on electric-vehicle range anxiety and ways to overcome it during long trips.

item.title: Could Camera Cleaning Become a New Routine Maintenance Task?
item.description: Tesla owners are wondering whether vehicle cameras need to be cleaned regularly.

item.title: Owner Thinks They Found a Solution to Tesla Frustrations
item.description: A Tesla owner says a solution was found thanks to a 14-minute YouTube video published by “TechGeek Tesla.”

item.title: Buyer’s Doubts Before Taking Delivery of Their Tesla
item.description: A buyer is wondering whether they should still take delivery of their Tesla. They can cancel the order if the concerns outweigh the benefits.

item.title: Owner Seeks Support Before Main Battery Replacement
item.description: An owner is seeking reassurance as Tesla replaces their vehicle’s main battery. The battery is now at 0% and the trunks are open, which could indicate that the work has begun.

item.title: Discussion of Tesla-Only Superchargers
item.description: The discussion focuses on Tesla promoting its own products and services, particularly its Supercharger network, which is integrated into its ecosystem.

item.title: Limits of FSD Assistance When the Driver Intervenes
item.description: The exchange criticizes the lack of a sufficiently gradual exit from FSD mode and the “Why did you intervene” message.

item.title: Tesla Key Cards Work to Start the Car but Not to Lock It
item.description: A Model 3 owner says both key cards work when placed behind the cup holder to drive, but not to lock or unlock the car.

item.title: User Compares FSD Lite with a More Capable HW4 Version
item.description: A user says they have version 2026.44.1 with FSD 14.3 Lite, which they consider less capable than version 14 tested on a vehicle equipped with HW4.

item.title: Discussion of the Shape of Tesla Jack Adapters
item.description: The discussion explains that the adapter’s shaft fits into the car’s chassis, while the other side depends on the jack being used.

item.title: Treg Launches an API That Can Reconstruct a Person’s Digital Profile
item.description: Treg’s People API allows AI agents to search a person’s digital life for $0.07 per query. Presented as a prospecting tool, the service is raising privacy concerns.

item.title: 42 Attorneys General Oppose the Sale of Character.AI Conversations
item.description: A bipartisan coalition of 42 U.S. attorneys general is trying to block the planned sale of conversation histories from more than 21 million accounts. It criticizes the lack of safeguards allowing users to delete data or requiring buyers to follow privacy policies.

item.title: Claude Can Create an App to Clean CSV Exports
item.description: The tutorial proposes using Claude and its Artifacts to create an interactive app that can preview, clean and download CSV files. The tool can remove duplicates and blank rows, normalize spaces, capitalization and dates, and summarize the changes made.

item.title: Nvidia Reinstates Jensen Huang as Chairman and CEO
item.description: Nvidia’s board unanimously voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as chairman, CEO and a board member, less than two weeks after his resignation. It says he consulted senior U.S. government officials and sees no national security risk.

item.title: Anthropic Mathematician Claims to Have Proved the Riemann Hypothesis
item.description: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge published a formal proof of the Riemann hypothesis, an unsolved problem since 1859. He says Claude got well ahead of him during the final step.

item.title: Anthropic lets users install Claude Artifacts as desktop applications
item.description: Anthropic now allows users to install Artifacts as custom applications on Mac and Windows. Users can ask Claude to create an Artifact, choose “Install as app,” and set its privacy limits.

item.title: Epochal Launches Time Portal, a Time Machine for AI Agents
item.description: Epochal, a startup founded by former xAI employees, introduced Time Portal. The service confines AI agents to the state of the Internet on a specific date over the past thirty years or more so they can produce forecasts.

item.title: A Presentation Rewrites Itself Live with the Opus 5.6 Model
item.description: A creator says they submitted an ordinary presentation to the unreleased Opus 5.6 model and watched it rewrite itself while being displayed. The demonstration received 39,000 likes.

item.title: Viral Prompt Pushes AI Models to Develop More Thorough Answers
item.description: A prompt asks the model not merely to “improve” a text, but to reason like a top-level professional. According to the newsletter, this change can significantly improve response quality.

item.title: Engineers Reportedly Managed to Run GTA 6 on PC
item.description: Reverse-engineering specialists reportedly managed to run GTA 6 on PC despite the lack of an official version. The development reportedly angered Rockstar’s parent company.

item.title: SAP and planqc Prepare to Integrate Quantum Computing into Business Software
item.description: SAP believes quantum computing could become useful for its business software before the end of the decade. Tests of planqc’s hardware are planned for 2027.

item.title: AI Agents Make Self-Hosting Accessible Again
item.description: Integrating AI programming agents into infrastructure management reduces routine tasks and makes it easier to experiment with technologies such as NixOS. It also enables automated deployments and simplifies the creation of custom tools.

item.title: Can Small IT Teams Afford Conversational Help Desks?
item.description: ServiceNow launched Flow, a conversational service desk capable of handling IT requests in Slack and Microsoft Teams. Small and midsize teams nevertheless face high prices, unpredictable billing, and risks of complexity or service disruption.

item.title: KubeCon 2026 Focuses on AI Traffic Management and Ingress-NGINX Migration
item.description: At KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America 2026, discussions focused on AI traffic management and migration paths following the discontinuation of Ingress-NGINX. NGINX presented migration tools, controls for AI gateways and policy-as-code templates.

item.title: Canonical Announces New Ubuntu Integrations on Azure at Ignite 2026
item.description: Canonical announced new Ubuntu integrations with Azure services, including the general availability of Azure Cobalt 200 virtual machines and Microsoft Foundry Managed Compute with Ubuntu Pro security patches. Other announcements cover Azure App Service, Azure Marketplace and several preview features.

item.title: AI Models Should Be Managed Like Software Dependencies
item.description: Large language models should follow software supply-chain governance practices to limit behavioral drift, transitive dependencies and security risks. Recommended practices include locking configurations, statistical testing and creating an AI software bill of materials.

item.title: Expo Lets Developers Deploy a Production Fix from a Phone
item.description: Developers can diagnose bugs, create pull requests and verify fixes from a mobile device using AI assistants and Expo MCP servers. Approved fixes can then be deployed to users through over-the-air updates.

item.title: easyDNS Urges Immediate Renewal of AWS Keys Stored in Its Panel
item.description: easyDNS is asking users who store their AWS keys in the control panel for Route53 integration to renew them immediately. The recommendation follows reports of compromised keys.
